bib.title: The Mythos of Model Interpretability
bib.venue: 2016 ICML Workshop on Human Interpretability in Machine Learning (WHI 2016); arXiv v3 6 Mar 2017

question: What does interpretability mean in supervised learning, why is it wanted, and which model properties and techniques are thought to confer it?
hypothesis: Interpretability is not a monolithic concept, and claims such as 'linear models are interpretable and deep nets are not' are ill-defined unless a specific notion is fixed.
contributions: Identifies that the term interpretability has no agreed meaning yet is used in a quasi-mathematical way

A first-step taxonomy of the desiderata (trust, causality, transferability, informativeness, fair and ethical decision-making) and of methods (transparency: simulatability, decomposability, algorithmic transparency; post-hoc: text, visualization, local explanation, explanation by example)
Notes that most interpretability techniques do not address contestability

results.claim: Interpretability has no formal technical meaning; the demand for it arises when the formal objective (test-set predictive performance) mismatches real-world costs in deployment.
results.setup: Conceptual argument over the literature; supervised learning only
results.quote:
At present, interpretability has no formal technical mean-
ing.

results.claim: Neither linear models, rule-based systems nor decision trees are intrinsically interpretable; high-dimensional models, unwieldy rule lists and deep trees can be less transparent than compact neural networks.
results.setup: Simulatability: a person can step through every calculation in reasonable time
results.quote:
we suggest
that neither linear models, rule-based systems, nor deci-
sion trees are intrinsically interpretable.

results.claim: Linear-model weights can be fragile to feature selection and preprocessing, so decomposability does not come free: the sign of the flu-vaccination association depends on whether age and immunodeficiency indicators are in the feature set.
results.quote:
The weights of a linear model might seem intuitive,
but they can be fragile with respect to feature selection and
pre-processing.

results.claim: Linear models are not strictly more interpretable than deep nets: they win on algorithmic transparency but lose simulatability with high-dimensional features and decomposability with heavily engineered ones.
results.setup: Depends on which notion of interpretability is used
results.quote:
Linear models are not strictly more interpretable
than deep neural networks

results.claim: Post-hoc interpretations can mislead, especially when optimized to placate subjective demands, since a model can be tuned to give plausible but misleading explanations.
results.setup: Argument by analogy to human justification of hiring and admissions decisions

results.claim: Saliency maps are local explanations only; moving a single pixel may give a very different map, unlike linear models which are global.
results.setup: Gradient of correct-class output with respect to the input
results.quote: The saliency map is a local explanation only.

results.claim: A pneumonia-risk model assigned lower risk to asthma patients because they received more aggressive treatment; deployed for triage it would invalidate itself.
results.setup: Reported example from Caruana et al. 2015
results.quote:
Caruana et al. (2015) de-
scribe a model trained to predict probability of death from
pneumonia that assigned less risk to patients if they also
had asthma.

results.claim: FICO credit models use logistic regression citing interpretability, yet several features (debt ratio, number of accounts) can be gamed by applicants, which may invalidate predictive power.
results.setup: Credit scoring; Fair Isaac Corporation 2011 technical report
results.quote:
The fact that individ-
uals actively and successfully game the rating system may
invalidate its predictive power.

results.claim: Claims about interpretability must fix a specific definition; transparency can be shown directly, post-hoc claims need a stated objective and evidence that the interpretation achieves it.
results.quote:
To be meaningful, any assertion
regarding interpretability should ﬁx a speciﬁc deﬁnition.

limits: No experiments or data; the argument is conceptual and by literature example
Scope limited to supervised learning; reinforcement learning is left as future work
Authors concede the transparency/post-hoc division is not absolute
Authors concede the right-to-explanation form and how to prove explanations correct remain open questions
Predates most later post-hoc methods (e.g. SHAP) and work on faithfulness of explanations
practices: Fix a specific definition of interpretability before claiming a model is interpretable (Sec 4.2).
For post-hoc interpretability, state a clear objective and show evidence the explanation achieves it (Sec 4.2).
Be wary of giving up predictive power for transparency without justification (Sec 4.3).
Be cautious of post-hoc explanations optimized to be plausible to humans (Sec 4.4).
Explanations to affected people should present falsifiable reasoning and allow contesting (Sec 2.5).

terms.definition: a person can contemplate the entire model at once and step through every calculation required to produce a prediction in reasonable time
each part of the model - each input, parameter, and calculation - admits an intuitive explanation
understanding at the level of the learning algorithm itself, e.g. the shape of the error surface and convergence to a unique solution
extracting information from learned models, e.g. text explanations, visualization, local explanations, explanation by example, without necessarily elucidating how the model works

figures.caption: Typically, evaluation metrics require only predictions and ground truth labels. When stakeholders additionally demand interpretability, we might infer the existence of desiderata that cannot be captured in this fashion.
figures.why: Shows why interpretation signals a gap between metric and real objective
